claims.head: Expect the Golden Knights to have the puck more
claims.body: The Golden Knights have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Red Wings around the middle. Expect the Golden Knights to spend more of the night in the Red Wings’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

DET.head: A slightly uphill night for the Red Wings
DET.body: Even though Detroit has home-ice advantage, Vegas has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Red Wings’ best way to tip it is keeping shots to a minimum.

VGK.head: The Golden Knights start a half-step ahead
VGK.body: Even though Detroit has home-ice advantage, Vegas has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Red Wings can still swing it if they keep shots to a minimum.

story.head: Kolesar meets his old team
paras: The Golden Knights (10-5-2) beat Pittsburgh 3-2 on Tuesday, while the Red Wings (7-6-3) lost 4-2 to Tampa Bay the same night. Going in, the Golden Knights are second in the Pacific (fifth in the NHL) and the Red Wings last in the Atlantic (tied for 16th).

The Golden Knights’ record (.647) is about what their chances are worth. The Red Wings have played better than their record (.531) says: their chances are worth about .598, and their finishing has held them back.

The Red Wings (1st) and the Golden Knights (2nd) both draw more penalties than they take. The Golden Knights have had shaky goaltending (31st). They also have the league’s best penalty kill (1st), and the Red Wings’ power play against their penalty killers is strength against strength. As for the Wings, they block more shots than almost anyone (2nd), but ice the puck a lot (30th). Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one.

Jack Eichel (7 G / 15 A / 22 P in 17 GP) leads the Golden Knights in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, and Mark Stone (10 G / 9 A / 19 P in 17 GP) has a team-high ten goals, tied for sixth in the NHL. For the Red Wings, Alex DeBrincat (7 G / 9 A / 16 P in 16 GP) leads the way in scoring. Viktor Arvidsson (8 G / 7 A / 15 P in 16 GP) has a team-high eight goals, with seven points in his last five games.
Adin Hill (6-2-0 / .895 SV% in 8 GS) is expected to go for Vegas. Daniil Tarasov (2-1-2 / .927 SV% in 4 GS) has been outstanding for Detroit and is expected to start.

At home, Todd McLellan likes to send Mazur, Dries and Kolesar out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Lavoie, Dowd and Gatcomb. Elsewhere, the Golden Knights usually control more of the chances than the Red Wings do.

Tomáš Hertl has six goals in six games against Detroit since 2023-24.
